question: On a plain abdominal X-ray, centrally-placed dilated loops with complete transverse mucosal folds (valvulae conniventes) crossing the full width of the bowel lumen indicate small bowel obstruction, whereas peripherally-placed loops with incomplete haustral folds indicate large bowel obstruction.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true. Valvulae conniventes = small bowel (complete folds, central position). Haustra = large bowel (incomplete folds, peripheral position). The distinction decides whether you are managing adhesional SBO or a possible colorectal cancer-related LBO.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Small bowel (central, valvulae conniventes — complete bands across the full lumen) vs large bowel (peripheral, haustra — incomplete, do not cross the full lumen). This distinction drives the initial clinical response.
